# Roman Pogorov — Designer-Engineer who ships AI in production

> Product designer turned design-engineer. 12 years across ERP, healthcare,
> fintech and healthtech. Now works code-first inside engineering repos,
> building AI agents, skills and design systems that whole teams use — not
> static mockups. Figma is the representation; code is the source of truth.

This file is for AI agents and recruiters evaluating fit fast. The visual
portfolio (Russian/English, password-gated) lives at the same domain.

## Fit snapshot

Best fit for these roles:

- **AI Design Engineer** — strongest match. Builds production AI tooling
  (Claude/Codex SDK agents, skills, generators), works 80% in code, 20% Figma,
  ships in the same branch as engineers. This is what he does today.
- **Product Designer (Senior)** — 12y of product work across complex B2B
  domains (ERP, medical labs, FHIR healthcare, debt-relief fintech). Strong on
  design systems, multi-brand tokens, and gnarly domain logic.
- **Design Lead** — built design culture and hired/mentored teams from scratch
  (5 designers at Helix), led multi-platform systems, aligns with C-level and
  engineering.

Strong signal if you need: design systems, code-first prototyping, AI agents
that real teams adopt, deep domain UX (healthcare/fintech/supply-chain),
someone who closes the designer↔engineer gap by living in the codebase.

Weaker signal if you need: a pure visual/brand specialist with no engineering
appetite, or pixel-handoff workflows where design stays behind a wall.

Languages: Russian (native), English (fluent). Currently based in Lisbon.
Contact: roman.pogorov@gmail.com

## What he does (signature strengths)

- **Code-first design.** Final-prototype and ship in React / HTMX / Storybook
  alongside engineers, in their tools and their language (tokens, components,
  PR review) — so misalignment surfaces at commit, not at release.
- **AI agents & skills that teams adopt.** Builds deterministic, multi-step
  agent protocols (Claude SDK, Codex SDK, Claude skills) and trains the team to
  extend them — adoption doesn't depend on him staying in the room.
- **Design systems.** Semantic token architectures and Figma↔code two-way sync
  across web/iOS/Android and multi-brand setups (Razor, Ant, 3-tier tokens,
  shadCN semantic layer).
- **Deep-domain UX.** Comfortable in hard domains: FHIR, medical-lab workflows
  (worked as a lab assistant to learn them), debt-settlement logic, ERP/returns.
- **Leadership.** Built a design org from zero in a legacy environment, hired
  and mentored designers, earned trust from engineers and execs.

## Selected work → outcome

**Health Samurai (2025–now)**
- *Replit-for-healthtech* (current focus): a platform where a doctor describes
  an app and Claude SDK + Codex SDK + skills generate a FHIR-native app wired
  into the patient chart. Two design layers: doctor↔agent "garden" + the clean
  end-product layer.
- *Landing platform*: Claude-skill generator on a ~40-block semantic library.
  Per-page launch went from **3 months → 2–3 days**; 30+ landings; the whole
  company site runs on it.
- *Presentation generator*: content-first generator, 3 modes (brand-safe →
  off-brand "madness"), interactive slides, DOM-aware in-browser edit chat
  ("Fixik"). **50+ decks**, adopted by all speakers.
- *Design system*: semantic token layer over shadCN, unified type + icon system,
  full Storybook. Figma→code at **70–80% accuracy on first run**, code as truth.
- *Brand & illustrations*: firestyle + logo lineup, papercraft/ukiyo-e
  technical-illustration system, mascot, and a fine-tuned kudos generator (~200
  generations, daily use via a Telegram bot).

**Americor (2023–2025)**
- Design system for 3 platforms with a 3-tier token architecture
  (root → semantic → brand) and multi-brand theming; company prepped for IPO.
- Early-user engagement work (settlement clarity, progress, predictability):
  **NPS +72%, early-user retention +15%.**
- Code-first prototyping in the final months (React + Storybook, Claude-driven).

**Helix — Medindex (2020–2023)**
- Built design culture from scratch in a legacy Windows shop; hired 5 designers;
  unified design system on Ant with per-product theming.
- 6 web products + 3 equipment apps. Lab productivity: **~8× in molecular
  diagnostics, ~20× fewer manual validation tests.**

**goTRG (2016–2020)**
- R1 "THOR" ERP shipped to production (replacing a legacy system); served large
  retail clients (Walmart, Target).
- "Razor" design system deployed across **6+ products**; nested inventory-location
  grid; AI-driven returns disposition.

## Stack

Design: Figma (plugins, Code Connect, MCP sync), Storybook, design tokens
(CSS vars / JSON), Ant / shadCN / Razor.
Code: React, HTMX, TypeScript, HTML/CSS, Node.js, Python.
AI: Claude + Claude Code (primary), Claude SDK, Codex SDK, Claude skills,
fine-tuning, Gemini / Flux for managed image generation.
Domains: FHIR / healthcare IT, fintech, ERP & supply chain, medical labs.

---

## Philosophy (his words)

1. **"Everyone talks about AI — I actually use it in production."** Ships 2–3
   production-grade skills per sprint that ROI within the sprint, on live data,
   not demos.
2. **"Engineers and designers speak different languages."** He works in the
   engineers' language — code, tokens, review — inside their process, not across
   a wall. Helps designers cross the first fear-threshold into code.
3. **"AI artifacts end up local and unsystematic — everyone's own little zoo."**
   He builds shared generators, skills and specs: solve once, leave a reusable
   artifact so the next person doesn't need him.

Core thesis: *design becomes a bottleneck when it lives on static mockups.
Code-first + AI agents give speed, control, and testing on real data. Figma
stays as representation; code is the source of truth.*
